rendered: NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated within a narrow pH window: 10 and 12[1]. The window is needed because the metal hydroxides do not precipitate together. Aluminum hydroxide starts to precipitate at a lower pH than nickel and iron hydroxides, which precipitate only beyond pH 6[2]. Simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is challenging because the hydroxide precipitates have different solubility products ("bility product Ksp of the resulting hydroxide precipitates"), so the aluminum-first precipitation narrows the usable window. In the reactor, NaOH is pumped in to hold the pH to maintain the pH to above 10[3], especially for nickel-rich materials. To make the powder, the outflow from the reactor is filtered, washed and dried to obtain the hydroxide precursors. These are mixed with a lithium source (a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.) before calcinating[4]), then calcined in an O2-rich environments at temperatures >600 °C[5]. After calcination, the NFA cathode powders are cast into electrodes by roll-to-roll slot-die coating ("calcination, the NFA cathode powders were cast into elec-").
